citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).
record_used: subject S002, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed), all 64 EEG channels, first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples) -- the SAME git-tracked root the sibling Hjorth case (eeg-hjorth-eegmmidb) uses.
pipeline: readRDS(eeg64_s002r02) -> PhysioAnalysis::bandPower(method='welch'): each channel's power spectral density by Welch's method (symmetric Hann window, nperseg=256, 50% overlap), integrated over the five EEG bands (delta 0.5-4, theta 4-8, alpha 8-13, beta 13-30, gamma 30-100 Hz). The reference re-computes every band power with scipy.signal.welch (symmetric Hann via fftbins=False, nperseg=256, noverlap=128, detrend=False, scaling='density') over the identical band indices, via reticulate. Deterministic.
note: The tracked input is agent/eval/data/hjorth-eeg/eeg64_s002r02.rds (64-channel eyes-closed EEG). Welch's method (1967) is the workhorse EEG spectral estimator: average the periodograms of overlapping windowed segments. This is the FIRST external-reference (scipy) certification of the bandPower Welch estimator -- it is already used across the EEG cases (Berger effect, alpha reactivity) for findings, but was never checked against the gold-standard scipy.signal.welch. bandPower(method='welch') reproduces scipy.signal.welch BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~7e-13 over all 64 channels x 5 bands) once the conventions are matched: the op's .getWindow uses a SYMMETRIC Hann (0.5*(1-cos(2*pi*k/(N-1))), so scipy needs fftbins=False), no per-segment detrend (scipy detrend=False), density scaling, one-sided doubling. The finding: relative alpha power is highest over the parieto-occipital region (peak at POz, 0.73; posterior mean 0.69 vs frontal 0.28) -- the classic eyes-closed posterior alpha rhythm, cross-consistent with the Hjorth case's low posterior mobility on the SAME data (alpha = slow oscillation = low mobility = high alpha power).
